intro: Daily success is a tiny ritual, not a heroic day. Morning glance, honest meals, evening skim — then stop obsessing.
buddyTip: Anchor logging to existing moments: after you sit down with the plate, not “when I remember tonight.”
mission: Complete today’s loop: morning check → log each meal → evening Foodiary skim.
why: Motivation is unreliable. Rituals survive busy weeks. A daily loop keeps Foodiary complete enough for Progress to mean something, without turning health into a second job.
Most “failures” are missing capture, not missing willpower. When breakfast goes unlogged, lunch estimates drift, and dinner becomes guesswork at midnight. Capture close to the meal protects honesty.
Daily wins are boring on purpose: protein at one meal, water logged, Progress glanced. Boredom is a feature — it means the system is becoming automatic.

what.lead: A full successful day has five quiet beats.
points: Morning — open Home; notice budget / Progress; optional weigh-in and water
Breakfast — log with Buddy; favour a protein-forward start when possible
Lunch — log again; if rushed, voice or photo beats skipping
Dinner — log what you actually ate; correct grams later if needed
Evening review — two-minute Foodiary skim; fix blank-kcal rows; one sentence win

misconceptions.myth: If I didn’t hit every target, the day was wasted.
misconceptions.truth: A logged imperfect day teaches Buddy. An unlogged “perfect” day teaches nothing.

misconceptions.myth: Evening review means analysing macros for an hour.
misconceptions.truth: Skim for missing meals and obvious errors. Deep analysis belongs to the weekly review.

how.lead: Keep the same time windows so the brain stops negotiating.
steps: Morning: 60 seconds on Home — weigh if that’s your habit, log water, note the day type (travel, training, rest)
Each meal: use the orange Log / Talk food control on Home — not Foodiary-first
Confirm Buddy’s estimate; adjust only when you know better
Evening: open Foodiary for today; fill gaps; avoid inventing precise grams you didn’t see
Write one daily win: “protein at lunch,” “walked,” “logged restaurant honestly”
how.buddyHelps: Home is the daily desk. Quick actions (camera, mic, water) reduce friction. Today’s Progress fills when logs carry real nutrition — that’s your feedback loop.

sections.title: Morning
paras: Keep mornings light. The job is orientation, not optimisation. If weigh-ins stress you, weigh less often — consistency of method beats daily drama.

sections.title: Meals
paras: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are equal citizens in the diary. Snacks count too. If you only log “clean” meals, Progress will lie optimistically.
When portions are unclear, a fair estimate logged now beats a perfect estimate never entered.

sections.title: Evening review & daily wins
paras: Ask: Did I capture the day? What one thing worked? What will I try tomorrow?
Then close the app. Sleep is recovery work — leave the spreadsheet brain at the door.

mistakes.quote: I’ll batch-log everything at 11pm from memory.
mistakes.why: Memory under-reports snacks and oils. Near-meal logging is more honest and less stressful.

mistakes.quote: I only log on good days so my average looks clean.
mistakes.why: Selective logging invents a fictional person. Buddy coaches the real one.

mistakes.quote: Daily success means crushing a huge deficit every day.
mistakes.why: Huge daily deficits often rebound. Daily success means ritual + protein/fibre awareness + sustainable energy.

encouragement: If you logged the day and learned one small thing, you won. Repeat tomorrow — that is the whole game.
